clue.text: Quite good-looking

definitions.meaning: as an adverb, ... well means fairly, as in ... good
attractive in appearance, especially in a delicate way

explanation.surface: A grudging compliment: someone is quite good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as an adverb meaning fairly and as an adjective meaning attractive.

clue.text: Cold sparkling cider for this fellow

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: sparkling suggests fizz and agitation, so the letters of cider are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A glass of chilled fizzy cider is offered to a particular man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkling' looks like a description of the drink, but it signals the anagram; the leftover single letter stands before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so any male bearer of it can be called this fellow.

clue.text: Greek character not in favour of Italian wine

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
opposed to something means being anti it

explanation.surface: A Greek person dislikes Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A red wine from the Tuscany region of Italy, a well-known example.

clue.text: Soldiers volunteering to protect a politician in Florida location

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the soldiers go round the other letters

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Volunteer troops guard a politician on a visit to Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on Florida's Gulf coast, a place in that state.

clue.text: Musical instrument storyteller mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: telling stories can mean telling lies, so a storyteller is a liar

explanation.surface: A bard mentions the instrument he plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storyteller' looks innocent but means a fibber, in the sense of telling stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harp-like stringed instrument of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Reject type of steak on display

parts.note: chuck is a cut of beef from the shoulder
something out is visible, as flowers are out

explanation.surface: A butcher's counter displays a steak nobody wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to throw away or discard, a synonym of reject.

clue.text: Plant book by Laurel's partner?

parts.note: Oliver Hardy partnered Stan Laurel in the comedy double act
an annual is a book published yearly, often for children

explanation.surface: A book written by the partner of the comedian Laurel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' is the definition; Laurel also looks like a plant but is Stan Laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that completes its life cycle in one year and survives frost, a gardening term.

clue.text: Helpers include American and British mates

indicators.note: one word including others means it holds them inside

parts.note: hands are workers or helpers, as farm hands
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A team of helpers includes friends from both sides of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate can be a spouse, and married men are spouses of their wives.

clue.text: Perhaps Othello extra speaking?

indicators.note: speaking says the word is judged by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: extra means additional, more

explanation.surface: Perhaps a stage production of Othello needs another walk-on actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extra' suggests a film or stage extra, fitting the Othello scene, but means more.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is described as a North African Muslim, an example of that people.

clue.text: Selected a hundred socks

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
hose is an old word for stockings and socks

explanation.surface: Someone picked out a hundred pairs of socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of choose, a synonym for picked or selected.

clue.text: Country folk taking part in operatic song

indicators.note: taking part in something means being within it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
folk means people, so men

explanation.surface: Country people join in singing an opera aria.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in the Caucasus region, an example of a country.

clue.text: Perceptive, like half of tutors and head of Eton

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

indicators.note: half of keeps the front three of the six letters of tutors, dropping the rest
head of keeps only the opening letter of the word Eton, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: A clever pupil is as sharp as half the tutors and the headmaster of Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English private school, so 'head of Eton' looks like its headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and quick to see how things are, a synonym of perceptive.

clue.text: Cycle accessory theology student found in auction

indicators.note: found in says these letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: an auction is a sale of goods
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree in theology

explanation.surface: A divinity student picks up a bike part at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: The seat on a bicycle is a part fitted to it, hence an accessory.

clue.text: Vegetable preserved in jam?

definitions.meaning: a vegetable kept in vinegar or brine
a jam is a predicament or tight spot

explanation.surface: Vegetables preserved in a jar of jam.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is food kept in vinegar; the other is a fix or difficult situation.

clue.text: African country makes our queen terribly irate

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the British queen's cipher

indicators.note: terribly suggests disorder, so the letters of irate are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An African nation makes the Queen terribly angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' reads as an intensifier for irate but is the anagram signal; 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation on the Red Sea coast of the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Acting award for Curtis, say

definitions.meaning: a prize for Broadway theatre achievement
... Curtis was a Hollywood actor, an example bearer of the name

explanation.surface: An acting prize goes to the film star Curtis.
explanation.definitionFit: The Broadway theatre prize and the first name of actor Tony Curtis.

clue.text: Very attractive part of hospital? Topping

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department
icing is a topping on a cake

explanation.surface: A wing of a hospital is praised as topping, old slang for excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like dated British slang for splendid but is a cake covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempting and alluring, so very attractive.

clue.text: Rewound part of Bob Marley film

indicators.note: Rewound says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tape of the reggae singer Bob Marley is rewound to replay part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sylvester Stallone action film series about a commando, one example of a movie.

clue.text: Reformed cheats, far from corrupt

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of cheats are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Cheats who have reformed are now far from corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and virtuous, the opposite of corrupt.

clue.text: Porter's work covering a twenty-four hour period?

definitions.meaning: a song by Cole Porter, the American songwriter
a full day comprises both its dark and light hours, hence round the clock

explanation.surface: A hotel porter works round the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cole Porter song title and a phrase for all the time.

clue.text: Near a record player a small coin is found

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, plays records
a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: A record player and a small coin are found close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record player' suggests a gramophone but means a disc jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying next to or close by, a synonym of near.

clue.text: Loved keeping rear of kitchen decorated

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so a letter is placed within

parts.note: adored means loved deeply

indicators.note: rear of takes the final letter of kitchen

explanation.surface: A loved home kept its kitchen back wall decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Embellished or ornamented, a synonym of decorated.

clue.text: More than once fellow fails to finish dance

indicators.note: more than once says the shortened word appears twice
failing to finish means the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: chap is informal for a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A man repeatedly fails to complete a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to finish' trims CHAP to CHA, which 'More than once' repeats.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: In Greek island there's a forge

indicators.note: In places the letter inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: On a Greek island there's a blacksmith's forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forge' looks like a noun, a smithy, but is the verb meaning make.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge something is to make or bring it into being.

clue.text: Film attempt to score goal

definitions.meaning: to film is to record on camera
in football, to kick at the goal

explanation.surface: A camera crew films a striker trying to score.
explanation.definitionFit: Both shooting a movie and shooting at goal use the same verb.

clue.text: Girl with no heart for exam, getting degree

indicators.note: no heart says the middle two letters of exam are removed

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A girl with no enthusiasm for an exam still gets her degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in Jane Austen's heroine.
